answer: Plates follow the state that issued them, not the state you live in, so your California plates need to come off the car. You'll need to return them to the California motor vehicle agency within 10 days. We'll give you the plate return receipt, form NW-PLT-1, which shows the car was sold. Also, because the car is registered in another state, you'll need an emissions certificate from a North Carolina inspection station before we can buy it at a North Carolina store, and you should bring your California registration.
